Per-class judge metrics

Source: R/confusion.R
confusion_metrics.Rd

Returns class support, predicted support, precision, and recall with humans treated as the reference. Unlike a hidden tibble attribute, this accessor is stable across ordinary serialization and reporting workflows.

Usage

confusion_metrics(
  x,
  label_levels = NULL,
  human_col = NULL,
  judge_col = NULL,
  conf_level = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A yourhonor_calibration object, a confusion tibble returned by confusion(), or a ratings data frame.

label_levels

Optional complete label universe in display order. For a calibration object or a confusion tibble it must contain every label observed there; the stored per-class rows are returned in that order, with zero-support rows for labels not seen.

human_col, judge_col

Passed to confusion() for a ratings data frame. Cannot be combined with a calibration object or a confusion tibble.

conf_level

Confidence level for the exact per-class intervals of a ratings data frame; NULL uses 0.95. A calibration object or a confusion tibble keeps the level its metrics were computed at, so conf_level cannot be combined with one: set it in calibrate_judge() or confusion() instead.

Value

A tibble with one row per label.

Examples

ratings <- data.frame(
  human = c("C", "C", "P", "I", "C", "P"),
  judge = c("C", "P", "P", "I", "C", "C")
)
confusion_metrics(ratings, label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   label support predicted precision precision_conf_low precision_conf_high
#>   <chr>   <int>     <int>     <dbl>              <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 I           1         1     1                 0.0250               1    
#> 2 P           2         2     0.5               0.0126               0.987
#> 3 C           3         3     0.667             0.0943               0.992
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: recall <dbl>, recall_conf_low <dbl>,
#> #   recall_conf_high <dbl>

# The same metrics from a confusion table.
tab <- confusion(ratings, label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"))
confusion_metrics(tab)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   label support predicted precision precision_conf_low precision_conf_high
#>   <chr>   <int>     <int>     <dbl>              <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 I           1         1     1                 0.0250               1    
#> 2 P           2         2     0.5               0.0126               0.987
#> 3 C           3         3     0.667             0.0943               0.992
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: recall <dbl>, recall_conf_low <dbl>,
#> #   recall_conf_high <dbl>
